front.title: Privacy-Preserving Verification of Linked-Dialog Relationships Across Trust Boundaries

abstract.t:
Agentic systems increasingly create, delegate, relay, and transform dialogs across multiple agents, protocols, services, and administrative trust boundaries. In these environments, a verifier may need to determine whether two dialogs are related without requiring unrestricted disclosure of their contents or relying exclusively on the assertions of an intermediary.
This document describes properties and a conceptual evaluation model for privacy-preserving verification of linked-dialog relationships across trust boundaries. It distinguishes dialog association from context propagation, relationship verification from authentication and authorization, and verification outcomes from assessments of evidence completeness.
The document also considers evidence scope, source positions, temporal references, intermediary continuity, lifecycle changes, identity binding, privacy, and evidence availability. It identifies requirements intended to help future protocol designs represent linked-dialog relationships in a way that can be independently evaluated while limiting unnecessary disclosure.
This document does not define a wire format, cryptographic mechanism, identifier format, transport binding, authorization protocol, audit-log structure, or completeness-proof mechanism. It provides terminology, design properties, and interoperability considerations for further discussion.
